findingDetails.title: Section 12's table is described as covering the thirteen registry questions but holds twelve rows, and the four resolved questions are named only in section 11
findingDetails.scopeProof: The intro is research.md:707; the twelve rows are :709-720; the four resolved seeds are :694-697; the registry counts were read from findings-registry.json openQuestions and resolvedQuestions, nine and four.
findingDetails.case: A reader who wants the four questions the run answered counts the table twelve rows, finds nine open and three pruned on the node cap, and cannot locate the four resolved ones without knowing to read section 11.
findingDetails.claim: The intro promises one table covering all thirteen registry questions; the table holds nine of them plus three pruned nodes, and the four resolved questions are only in section 11.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Searched the document for the four resolved questions by name and found them at research.md:694-697, so the information is present but in another section.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Section 11 is the natural home for the resolved seeds, so the split is deliberate and the intro sentence is only loose.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: A sentence in section 12 that says the table covers the nine open questions and the three pruned nodes, with the resolved seeds in section 11.
